A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UNSURE research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated in v3.

before.justification: V1 reports original denoising and reconstruction experiments on MNIST, DIV2K, LIDC and FastMRI, including quantitative results and reconstructed images in Section 4.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds a real Cryo-EM denoising experiment with qualitative results in Section 5 and Figure 5.

M1.justification: The saddle-point training procedure, score-based alternative, noise extensions and inverse-problem adaptation are retained. DF is renamed ZED. Corrected main-text objectives align with formulations already present in v1's appendices; Cryo-EM uses the existing PG-UNSURE method.

E1.justification: V3 adds Cryo-EM data from Topaz-EM: five 7676 × 7420 images with an unknown noise distribution. This substantially extends coverage to biological microscopy and naturally acquired noise, beyond the prescribed corruptions used previously. All earlier datasets and tasks remain.

E2.justification: Noise2Noise becomes an evaluated comparator in the new Cryo-EM experiment; v1 only discussed it as related work. Existing comparator sets remain unchanged. The LIDC prose changes Noise2Void to Noise2Inverse, matching the comparator already named in v1's table and figure.

E3.justification: The new Cryo-EM experiment introduces five-image evaluation and training with 512 × 512 crops. PG-UNSURE receives whole-video averages, whereas Noise2Noise uses half-video averages to form pairs, giving different input SNRs. Settings for the retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 5 adds a qualitative Cryo-EM case study examining residual artifacts through enlarged image regions. Existing kernel-size sensitivity, MNIST convergence and noise-estimation comparisons, the DRUNet theory check and toy-distribution analyses are retained; relocating the toy examples adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: The retained PSNR tables use identical ± reporting. V3 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new Cryo-EM results are qualitative and provide no additional uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V1 Tables 2–5 match v3 Tables 1–4; the toy results and retained plots also remain unchanged. V3 adds a finding of fewer Cryo-EM artifacts than Noise2Noise under unequal input SNRs. Figure 2's accompanying wording corrects the reported sub-1-dB gap from all noise levels to most.

T1.justification: Theorem 3 gains explicit Gaussian-convolution and linearly independent basis assumptions. Appendix A adds strong-duality and Gram-matrix invertibility arguments. Equation 6 gains the missing 1/n normalization, and the main covariance and Poisson-Gaussian objectives receive corrections consistent with earlier appendix formulations.

C1.justification: Contribution 2 explicitly narrows the advertised exponential-family extension to certain distributions, matching the restricted subclass already treated mathematically. The central claims about unknown-noise-level learning, the robustness-expressivity trade-off and self-supervised performance remain.

C2.justification: V3 removes the blind-deblurring interpretation, explicitly identifies the theory's infinite-data scope and explains the covariance-family dimension trade-off. It also acknowledges PG-UNSURE's higher-SNR input in the Cryo-EM comparison. The stated perceptual-loss and computational limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The Cryo-EM description supplies its data source, frame-averaging procedure, four-scale bias-free U-Net, crop size and Adam learning rate of 5 × 10^-4. Earlier implementation details and the paper's code link are retained. Algorithm 1 is relocated rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: V3 adds empirical-Bayes positioning and references to Robbins and Efron, including a novelty claim concerning partially unknown noise distributions. It removes the residual-whiteness discussion and blind-deconvolution references, and adds references supporting Cryo-EM evaluation and strong duality. Most related-work positioning remains.

P1.justification: V3 substantially reorganizes the narrative: background and UNSURE become separate sections, examples and exponential-family material move to dedicated appendices, and pseudocode moves to experimental details. It also revises the title and replaces DF terminology with ZED throughout. Some Appendix A references remain stale after relocation.

P2.justification: V3 adds a Cryo-EM montage with enlarged regions, clarifies Figure 1 labels, updates legends and adjusts figure sizes and page spacing. The toy figure/table and pseudocode move to appendices. Existing plot designs, reconstruction images and numerical table structures are otherwise preserved.

improvement.justification: V3 improves precision through explicit theorem assumptions, added duality and invertibility reasoning, and mathematical corrections. The real-noise Cryo-EM demonstration broadens practical evidence, but its qualitative results and unequal input SNRs limit the comparative conclusion. Existing quantitative evidence is unchanged, and restructuring introduces stale appendix references. These support a limited overall improvement.
